gradeScale: Star ratings from 1 to 5 stars (5 = phenomenal / top tier benchmark, 4 = very solid recommendation, 3 = average / typical for price, 2 = flawed / hard to recommend, 1 = poor). Scores are officially published on his squig.link database and review videos; quotes are verbatim excerpts from his YouTube review captions.

entries.name: Binary Acoustics x Gizaudio Chopin
entries.verdict: Mark (Super* Review) gives it a full 5/5 stars; named the best collab IEM in years with meaty, physical sub-bass, clean mids, and crisp, phenomenal vocal reproduction.
entries.quote: out of five stars you may not be surprised to hear uh I'm going to give it a full five stars I love the chopan

entries.name: TruthEar Hexa
entries.verdict: Mark (Super* Review) rates it 5/5 stars; a no-brainer recommendation at $80 for neutral tuning enthusiasts, offering clean mid-range focus and great ergonomics.
entries.quote: You already know I'm giving this thing five stars out of five. I think that at even double the price of this IM, it would be like an easy recommendation. At 80 bucks, it's a no-brainer.

entries.name: Truthear x Crinacle Zero: RED
entries.verdict: Mark (Super* Review) gives it 4/5 stars; a sophisticated, well-balanced sound signature with clean mid-range focus and satisfying bass punch, plus an impedance adapter for extra low end.
entries.quote: overall, I think it is a very well balanced sound signature compared to a lot of V-shaped sound signatures that you typically get at around this price range. The mid-range is very, very well focused on this set, but it still has a pleasant bass presence that you can dial up with the impedance adapter if you choose.

entries.name: Moondrop Blessing 3
entries.verdict: Mark (Super* Review) gives it an easy 5/5 stars; an impressive technical upgrade over the Blessing 2 with dual-DD punch and crystal-clear upper midrange detail.
entries.quote: honestly, I can't I can't deny that this is still an upgrade over the Blessing 2. And so, it's an easy five stars out of five for me.

entries.name: Moondrop Variations
entries.verdict: Mark (Super* Review) gives it 4/5 stars; an outstanding technical tribrid with clean sub-bass rumble, natural mids, and sparkling electrostatic treble that matches his personal tonal preferences.
entries.quote: And I struggled with this, but honestly, out of five stars, I'm going to go ahead and give the Moon Drop Variations four stars.

entries.name: Sennheiser IE 200
entries.verdict: Mark (Super* Review) rates it 3/5 stars; an improvement over the IE 300 with comfortable shells, but lacking the technical performance of top peers in its price bracket and hindered by poor stock accessories.
entries.quote: in its price range. And I think against stuff in its price range, the IE200 is I it's I give it three stars out of five.

entries.name: Sennheiser IE600
entries.verdict: Mark (Super* Review) gives it an enthusiastic 5/5 stars; praised as endgame single dynamic driver performance with authoritative bass texture and phenomenal clarity in a tiny titanium shell.
entries.quote: This completely blew away my past expectations of Sennheiser IEMs. Incredible resolution, deep textured bass from a single dynamic driver, and endgame performance in a tiny comfortable shell.

entries.name: 7Hz Timeless
entries.verdict: Mark (Super* Review) rates it 3/5 stars; impressive planar transient speed and micro-detail resolution, but held back by softer bass impact and aggressive treble peaks.
entries.quote: Out of five stars I give the 7Hz Timeless three stars. Impressive planar speed and detail retrieval, but the bass quality and treble control leave something to be desired.

entries.name: Moondrop x Crinacle DUSK
entries.verdict: Mark (Super* Review) gives it a full 5/5 stars; an exceptional tribrid benchmark with reference DSP tuning perfection, punchy dual dynamic drivers, and smooth planar treble extension.
entries.quote: Out of five stars it is an easy five stars for the Dusk. The default DSP tuning is essentially reference perfection with incredible bass slam, natural mids, and smooth planar treble.

entries.name: TANGZU Wan'er S.G
entries.verdict: Mark (Super* Review) gives it 3/5 stars; a decent $20 set with pleasant musical tonality and warm bass, but resolving capability and build typical of its ultra-budget tier.
entries.quote: Not even necessarily a bad set. It's just it sounds like a $20 set. It sounds like roughly what I would expect at this price range.

entries.name: 7Hz Salnotes Zero
entries.verdict: Mark (Super* Review) rates it 4/5 stars; praise for its clean neutral tonality, textured vocals, tight bass attack, and crisp transient response under $25.
entries.quote: vocals have a lot more texture on the sound zero. I think even like the bass attack sounds a little bit tighter and I attribute that somewhat to the treble performance.

entries.name: AFUL Performer 8
entries.verdict: Mark (Super* Review) gives it 4/5 stars; a compelling package at $380 offering a mostly neutral signature with a tasteful sub-bass boost and slightly bright, articulate treble.
entries.quote: stars I think at 380 bucks this is a pretty compelling little package I I give it four stars out of five

entries.name: AFUL Acoustics Performer 5+2
entries.verdict: Mark (Super* Review) rates it 4/5 stars; engaging hybrid performance with punchy low-end dynamics and articulate planar micro-detail up top.
entries.quote: I'm going to give the Performer 5+2 four stars out of five. Very engaging hybrid performance with punchy low-end dynamics and nice planar micro-detail up top.

entries.name: 7th Acoustics Supernova
entries.verdict: Mark (Super* Review) awards it all 5/5 stars; praised for peerless vocal timbre, smooth effortless treble, and multi-BA resolution on par with the Moondrop S8.
entries.quote: Look, this probably shouldn't be a surprise, but I'm gonna go ahead and give Seven Acoustic Supernova all five of my stars.

entries.name: ThieAudio Monarch MKII
entries.verdict: Mark (Super* Review) gives it a solid 4/5 stars; high-tier tribrid with stellar sub-bass extension and clarity, though held back from 5 stars by its bulky shell and fit constraints.
entries.quote: That said, I will still give this thing a very solid four stars out of five. Just just take it with the warning that it might not fit your ear

entries.name: Moondrop Chu 2
entries.verdict: Mark (Super* Review) rates it 4/5 stars; solid sound with pleasant bass and an excellent metal form factor with detachable cable that punches above its entry-level price.
entries.quote: physical form factor however I would say is excellent for the price range and because of that I'd say you know that's good enough for four stars for me

entries.name: Moondrop Aria
entries.verdict: Mark (Super* Review) gives it 4/5 stars; an easy recommendation at $80 with an all-purpose Harman-warm tuning that obsoleted the Starfield.
entries.quote: And so out of five stars, I got to give the Moonrop Arya four stars. Very, very solid. IM. This is going to be a really easy recommendation

entries.name: Moondrop KATO
entries.verdict: Mark (Super* Review) awards it all 5/5 stars; a top pick at $190 with refined single dynamic driver timbre, beautiful build, and clean, controlled vocal definition.
entries.quote: Frankly, I got to give this thing one, two, three, four, all five of my stars. The Moon Drop KO for 190 bucks. This is definitely one of the top picks at this price range.

entries.name: Letshuoer s12 Ultra
entries.verdict: Mark (Super* Review) rates it 4/5 stars; named his favorite planar IEM under $200 with faster planar transients, detailed layering, and well-controlled treble.
entries.quote: The S12 Ultra. Um finally, my new favorite planar IEM under 200 bucks. And for that, we're going to give it a solid four stars out of five.

entries.name: Moondrop LAN
entries.verdict: Mark (Super* Review) gives it 5/5 stars; a mature, competently tuned sub-$50 single dynamic driver that remained a continuous favorite long after initial review.
entries.quote: competently mature tuned IEM that you can get for around 40, 45 dollars, and that is still pretty stinking rare. It's also built nice, it looks nice.

entries.name: Kiwi Ears Cadenza
entries.verdict: Mark (Super* Review) gives it a solid 4/5 stars; a smooth, musical mild V-shape tuning with punchy bass attack and fantastic 3D vocal positioning in a handsome resin shell under $35.
entries.quote: It's not bad. It's not irritating. This is a nice easy listen in a lot of ways. And I love the the the form factor. The build on this is actually really good. For 35 bucks, not too shabby. Um, honestly, the Kiwi ears cadenza, I think I'm gonna get give it a solid four stars out of five.

entries.name: TinHiFi C2
entries.verdict: Mark (Super* Review) awards it all 5/5 stars and crowns it the winner of Concha Combat 2022; outstanding resolution, durable all-metal shell, and class-leading technical performance under $30.
entries.quote: This is my first like fivestar budget set in a long time. I think the C2 is pretty outstanding. I can't think of any reason to not recommend this set. The cable is fine. Um but it's also replaceable if you want to get a different cable. Uh, and then the build on this is actually pretty nice for a $30 IM.

entries.name: Moondrop Chu
entries.verdict: Mark (Super* Review) rates it 4/5 stars; lauded for exceptional sub-$20 tonal balance and clean midrange, though slightly held back by its fixed non-detachable cable.
entries.quote: Moon Drop Chew, unfortunately, now is exiting our tournament. Uh, if this cable wasn't so awful, I would have higher, I don't know, higher frequency of recommending the set, but it's still quite good. So, Moonrop 2, still four stars out of five.

entries.name: Moondrop QUARKS DSP
entries.verdict: Mark (Super* Review) rates it 3/5 stars; tiny bullet form factor with integrated USB-C DAC/DSP tuning, but limited resolution and noticeable treble roll-off.
entries.quote: out of five stars, H. It's pretty cheap. It's 15 bucks. It fits nice, but I don't know. I still think that's probably like a three star

entries.name: Tanchjim Zero
entries.verdict: Mark (Super* Review) gives it 3/5 stars; bright vocal-forward tuning with punchy bass attack and compact bullet shells, but somewhat skewed upper midrange balance.
entries.quote: You know, I didn't give this one a review earlier this year, but the Tantum Zero, this is not a bad set. It's got nice base attack, decent form factor, but it's not quite there. So, I'm going to give it three stars out of five.

entries.name: Tanchjim Ola
entries.verdict: Mark (Super* Review) rates it 3/5 stars; clear vocal-centric mid-range with inoffensive highs, but undermined by lackluster bass impact and awkward ergonomics.
entries.quote: the Ton Jim Ola, unfortunately, is going to leave us. I already did do a review of this one, but I will just reiterate it for posterity sake. This is a three out of five. It's a decent little set. It's kind of inoffensive, except it just doesn't fit that well, and the base is really pretty lackluster, unfortunately.

entries.name: HIDIZS MP145
entries.verdict: Mark (Super* Review) rates it 2/5 stars; planar IEM with decent bass and tuning filters, but hindered by thinner vocal body, excessive bulk, and harsh treble timbre.
entries.quote: Hidizs MP145. I also don't love this one this earphone. I think that I have fewer issues with the treble. Maybe, if I'm squinting. Um I don't The overall tonality is a little bit on the thinner side, so I don't know. In some ways, they kind of just trade balance or they trade blows in terms of overall tonality, but I do find that the treble is less nasty on the MP145. So, you get you get two stars,

entries.name: Letshuoer S12
entries.verdict: Mark (Super* Review) rates it 4/5 stars; celebrated as his benchmark favorite sub-$200 planar IEM for 5 straight years, offering blazing planar speed and punchy dynamics in a compact metal shell.
entries.quote: This is the original Letshuo S12 and it's actually the first planar IEM I ever heard way back 5 years ago and for the past 5 years it's honestly still been my favorite sub $200 planar IEM. That is until now because one of these three planars is now finally better.
